title: The oldest message in a bottle
text: When a fisherman dragged a battered bottle {{1}} the North Sea, he found {{2}} he assumed was rubbish. In fact, it contained the {{3}} known message in a bottle, dropped from a German research vessel in 1908. The note asked the finder to return it {{4}} the address given, promising a small reward. Such bottles were used {{5}} scientists to chart ocean currents; each returned note mapped {{6}} the sea carries floating objects. The fisherman's reward, adjusted for inflation, turned {{7}} to be a crate of beer. The bottle now sits in a museum, {{8}} it attracts a steady stream of curious visitors.

gaps.explanation: 'dragged from the sea' — out of the water.
'what' = the thing that — object of found.
'turn out to be' = prove to be.
